title: Malicious service installation and encoded PowerShell execution on WORKSTATION6
summary: A new service PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX was installed by user pgustavo on WORKSTATION6 immediately after a network logon from 172.18.39.5. The service executes an encoded PowerShell command that disables security controls (ScriptBlockLogging, AMSI), downloads and runs code from external IP 10.10.10.5 (suspicious, not in company network), and launches whoami.exe for reconnaissance. User pgustavo is a lab user normally on WORKSTATION5, making this anomalous activity.
evidence: Service PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX installed at 06:57:48.992 by pgustavo on WORKSTATION6
Encoded PowerShell command -enc flag present, decoded content shows attempts to disable ScriptBlockLogging and AMSI
PowerShell connected to external IP 10.10.10.5:80 within 3 seconds of execution
IP 10.10.10.5 rated suspicious (private address, not in company known ranges)
User pgustavo normally logs into WORKSTATION5, not WORKSTATION6
Process chain: services.exe -> cmd.exe -> powershell -enc -> whoami.exe
Decoded command contains nested base64, downloads from web, uses proxy credentials

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 from network immediately
Terminate malicious service PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX
Reset pgustavo's credentials and verify account compromise
Block connectivity to IP 10.10.10.5 at perimeter firewall
Audit all services on WORKSTATION6 for additional persistence mechanisms
Review pgustavo's login history and other workstation access patterns

title: Malicious encoded PowerShell execution on WORKSTATION6 with defense evasion and web download

The command decoded to disable script block logging, bypass AMSI, and download additional payload from external IP 10.10.10.5 (suspicious, not in company network). This continues the attack chain from ALERT-001.

title: Legitimate Azure Guest Agent lsass access on WORKSTATION5
summary: The alert triggered on CollectGuestLogs.exe, a legitimate Microsoft Azure Guest Agent component (v2.7.41491.993), reading lsass.exe memory during normal diagnostic operations. The process chain (WaAppAgent.exe → CollectGuestLogs.exe → cmd.exe) and access rights (0x1410 = FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES | SYNCHRONIZE) are consistent with Azure diagnostics, not credential dumping. No Mimikatz indicators, encoded commands, or suspicious user behavior observed.
evidence: CollectGuestLogs.exe is a legitimate Azure Guest Agent component (confirmed by path and version timestamp 2020-09-17)
Process chain: WaAppAgent.exe → CollectGuestLogs.exe → cmd.exe → conhost.exe (standard Windows console hierarchy)
Access rights 0x1410 = FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES (0x1000) | SYNCHRONIZE (0x410), not full memory dump rights typical of credential theft
No encoded PowerShell, suspicious IPs, or user anomalies detected
Prior alerts ALERT-001/002/003 are on WORKSTATION6; this alert is on WORKSTATION5 - separate host
related_to_prior: None - this alert is on WORKSTATION5 while prior findings ALERT-001/002/003 are on WORKSTATION6

recommended_actions.action: Close alert as false positive - legitimate Azure Guest Agent diagnostic activity
No containment required
Monitor for future lsass access from this agent if pattern changes
